title: Public Toilet Seats Have That Gap Because Of A Rulebook
hook: An inconsistency between home and public fixtures, explained by a rulebook.

cast.note: Keep it clean and matter-of-fact. Gus is the code official. Nothing here is a toilet joke.

scenes.from: Public toilet seats have a gap
scenes.note: TONE: plainly, without smirking. The comparison is the hook, not the subject.

beats.action: a public restroom stall; the open-front seat draws in clean outline
the gap at the front circles teal
a closed home seat draws beside it; the two shapes compare directly

scenes.note: One beat. A book lands. That is the whole scene.

beats.action: a plain code book drops onto frame and opens

scenes.note: Gus stamps the clause. Note: codes are ADOPTED by jurisdictions, not federal law — the stamp says CODE, not LAW.

beats.action: a clause highlights on the open page: open-front seats, public use
Gus stamps the clause once, hard
a date line runs back across five decades behind the page
the page turns to the clause and settles
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: Gus squares the page edge with one finger
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.from: The gap keeps the seat clear
scenes.note: The functional reason, drawn as a plain contact-zone diagram. No bodies.

beats.action: the seat outline shows a shaded contact zone
the gap removes the seat from that zone; the shading pulls back
a long queue of figures files past the same seat, one after another
the shaded contact zone pulses once on the seat outline
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

beats.action: the closed seat shows a low front trough; the open seat has nowhere for it to gather
the closed seat outline tilts to show its front trough
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: The reframe: not cheapness, a requirement. Hard cut.

beats.action: a CHEAP label appears over the seat and crosses out
the code stamp lands over it instead; hard cut
